title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 34-36): M is a motive over R, or the Tannakian subcategory it generates. Its motivic Galois group is G = Aut⊗(T_B) over Q. The 'real Frobenius' f_∞ ∈ G(Q), with f_∞² = 1, is induced by complex conjugation on X(C). The period torsor is P = Isom⊗(T_B⊗R, T_DR), a G_R-torsor, and α ∈ P(C) is the canonical comparison isomorphism (Betti ⊗ C ≅ de Rham ⊗ C). The Hodge (Deligne-torus) homomorphism is j : S = Res_{C/R}G_m → G_R. Its two cocharacters over C are f_1 and f_2, with f_1·f_2 the weight cocharacter (written 'i', perhaps 'w'). The relation f_∞ j(λ) f_∞^{-1} = j(λ̄) gives f_∞ f_1 f_∞ = f_2.

Step 1. Complex conjugation acts on α by ᾱ = f_∞ α. So the point α of the R-scheme P is real, i.e. its residue field R(α) is R, iff f_∞ = 1 (on the category generated by M). Otherwise R(α) = C.

Step 2. Let ε : G → G_m be the Tate character (the action on Q(1)). Then ε(f_∞) = -1, because conjugation reverses the orientation of P¹(C) and so acts by -1 on H²(P¹) = Q(-1). Equivalently, the period 2πi of Q(1) is purely imaginary. Hence if M's category contains the Tate motive, f_∞ ≠ 1 and R(α) = C.

Step 3. In general, f_∞ = 1 forces f_1 = f_2 (so f_1 = f_2 = ½ weight). Then the Hodge structure is purely of type (p,p), and its Mumford-Tate group is the image of f_1. Granting the Hodge conjecture, G° equals the Mumford-Tate group, so G° = Im f_1 (G_m or trivial). Grothendieck adds that G = G° here: the component group is generated by f_∞, which is now trivial. So M is generated by some Q(-n), and f_∞ = (-1)^n on Q(-n) forces n even.

Conclusion (modulo the Hodge conjecture): f_∞ = 1 ⇔ R(α) = R ⇔ M is generated by Q(-2n) for some n ≥ 0 ⇔ G ≅ G_m or G = {e}. That is, the period torsor of a motive over R has its canonical point real only for even Tate motives.

Crossed-out and marginal fragments: a parenthetical NB about disconnected G (G = G_m/μ_n with f_∞ ∉ G°(Q)), and a boxed NB that is unclear, possibly saying f_∞ can only be trivial/central when G° = Im f_1. The page serves Grothendieck's study of motives over R and of the real structure of the period torsor. The next page formalises this as a twisted form of G via the cocycle f_∞.
errors: Minor: the first argument (contains Tate ⇒ f_∞≠1) is unconditional, but the converse direction relies on the Hodge conjecture (as Grothendieck notes) and also on G/G° being generated by f_∞ (a motivic-Galois/Tate-type assumption over R), which is only sketched ('ici G = G° car ...').

Statement 'f_1=f_2=½ i' is notational: means both Hodge cocharacters equal half the weight cocharacter, which only makes sense on the level of weights (all weights even); not literally a division of cocharacters.

Phrasing 'f_∞ = 1' must be read on the Tannakian subcategory generated by M (on Artin motive Spec C over R, f_∞ ≠ 1 without any Tate twist); the page handles this only via the crossed-out disconnected-G remark.

ideas.what: Real Frobenius f_∞ as an element of the motivic Galois group G(Q) with f_∞²=1, and complex conjugation of the period point α given by ᾱ = f_∞α
ideas.modern_name: F_∞ / real structure on the period torsor of motives over R
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Valeurs de fonctions L et périodes d'intégrales, 1979); Deligne–Milne, Tannakian categories (1982)

ideas.what: Period torsor P = Isom⊗(T_B⊗R, T_DR) and field of definition of its canonical point
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck period torsor / period conjecture setup
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (reported by André, Une introduction aux motifs, 2004); Kontsevich–Zagier
ideas.where_published: Only a footnote-level mention in Grothendieck's published work (period conjecture); details known via André

ideas.what: Tate character evaluated on F_∞ is -1 (2πi purely imaginary); hence the period torsor of a motive containing Q(1) has no real canonical point
Classification (mod Hodge conjecture) of motives over R whose real Frobenius is trivial: exactly the even Tate motives, G ≅ G_m or trivial
ideas.modern_name: Hodge–Tate type with trivial F_∞ / Mumford–Tate group argument

missed.claim: Historical: the notes appear to predate Deligne's 1979 treatment. They already treat the real Frobenius as a ⊗-automorphism of the Betti fibre functor and describe the real structure of the period torsor by the Z/2-cocycle f_∞. They also give the twisted descent int(f_∞)×σ on G_C and the compatibility f_∞ j(λ) f_∞^{-1} = j(λ̄) with the Hodge torus.
missed.quote: L'élément α ∈ P(C) est relié à f_∞ par ᾱ = f_∞ α
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck's early (c. 1969–72) Tannakian treatment of motives over R and periods, relevant for crediting the period-torsor formalism; mathematically standard today.

deep.surprise_reason: Mathematically elementary and now standard (Deligne 1979, Deligne–Milne 1982). The interest is historical: an early, explicit Tannakian treatment by Grothendieck of the real structure of the period torsor and of F_∞ on motives over R.
transcription_corrections: 'f_1 = f_2 = ½ i' — 'i' is most likely Grothendieck's notation for the weight cocharacter (f_1·f_2 = i), not the imaginary unit.
'donc f_∞ a priori' — the braced annotation links f_∞ to the equivalence f_∞=1 ⇔ α∈P(R) ⇔ R(α)=R.
'si M ne contient pas le motif de Tate' is followed by '...donc en vertu de la conj. de Hodge, il faut que G° = Im f_1' (the '{e}' was an overwritten alternative).
In the final NB, 'Q(2)' is probably meant as Q(-2) (even Tate twist). The underlined word read as 'autre' may be 'central' or '1'.
Left margin reads 'moyennant conj. de Hodge', attached to the final equivalence.
